wiki_text: On 21 January 2026, Hanwha Ocean signed a strategic memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Fermeuse Energy to jointly advance the proposed Newfoundland and Labrador (Fermeuse) LNG export project. Under the MOU, Hanwha Ocean becomes a long-term strategic partner supporting the project across the full LNG value chain — conceptual studies, pre-FEED engineering, development, financing, shipbuilding and LNG logistics. Hanwha framed the involvement as part of a broader Canadian industrial commitment linked to the Canadian Patrol Submarine Project (CPSP). The arrangement is a partnership/MOU, not an announced equity stake, so it does not by itself change the project's ownership; the project remains at proposed status with no FID.

Coverage of the September 2025 Fermeuse/Crown LNG announcement describes a CAD $12-15 billion liquefaction hub at the Fermeuse marine supply base intended to monetize ~9.7 Tcf of offshore associated gas in the Jeanne d'Arc Basin, with a stated aspiration of up to ~10 million tonnes per year of LNG and a possible start-up around 2031. The ~10 mtpa figure is a developer aspiration reported in trade press, not a confirmed nameplate from a regulatory filing, and should not be entered as a GEM Capacity value without primary confirmation. Crown LNG (US-listed; same CEO, Swapan Kataria, as Fermeuse) would supply its Norwegian gravity-based-structure (GBS) liquefaction design.

topic: Sponsor rename (Pieridae -> Cavvy Energy) and 2024 asset sale
wiki_text: Pieridae Energy Limited — the original Goldboro LNG developer — formally changed its name to Cavvy Energy Ltd. (TSX: CVVY) on 9 May 2025 after a 8 May 2025 shareholder vote, as part of a pivot away from East Coast LNG. Before the rename, Pieridae had already abandoned Goldboro (announced Nov 2023) and completed the sale of its Goldboro Nova Scotia assets (land and construction permit) in July 2024 for CAN$12 million to a Nova Scotia numbered company tied to Sam Roch-Perks of Ireland's Simply Blue Group, which had signalled interest in a sustainable-aviation-fuel / ocean-energy use of the site. As a result, the GEM owner entry 'Cavvy Energy Ltd' reflects the renamed former developer, but Cavvy no longer holds the Goldboro assets.
